title: Fulfilling Our Duties to Allah
intro: What Allah has asked of us, and what helps us to do it.

learn.text: O you who have believed, obey Allah…

learn.html: Allah, the Most High, has given Muslim men and women certain duties. We should do them regularly and keep doing them steadily. Some of these duties are fard – strict Islamic duties. They are:

items: Shahadah – declaring that we belong to Islam
Sawm (fasting) – keeping away from food, drink and other bodily pleasures
Hajj – the pilgrimage to the Ka‘bah and other holy places

learn.html: Besides these main duties there are others that are wajib. They are not commanded as strictly as fard: praying the witr prayer and the Eid prayer, offering the qurbani sacrifice, and giving sadaqat al-fitr before the Eid prayer.

When a believer fulfils his duties to Allah (SWT), he benefits in this world – the dunya – and in the next world – the akhirah. Allah (SWT) does not need us to do these duties. He commanded them because they make our hearts pure and our character better.

Every Islamic duty teaches us something – it helps us become better and more complete people. Salah keeps us away from what is bad, fasting makes us more mindful of Allah, zakah makes us more generous, and Hajj makes believers better in character. By fulfilling our duties to Allah (SWT) we become Allah’s servants – and being Allah’s servant means being the freest being on Earth.

learn.text: What helps us to fulfil our duties

learn.title: Believe in Allah (SWT) firmly, without doubt
learn.html: Muhammad (SAW) taught us to believe in Allah as if we see Him – because even though we do not see Him, He truly sees us.

quran.text: O you who have believed, believe in Allah…

learn.title: Love Him
learn.html: Love for Allah (SWT) is stronger and greater than any other love.

quran.text: And [yet], among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals [to Him]. They love them as they [should] love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah.

learn.title: Remember Him (dhikr)
learn.html: We should remember Allah all the time. Remembering Allah comes from always being aware of Him.

quran.text: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance and exalt Him morning and afternoon.

learn.title: Thank Him for His blessings
learn.html: Allah’s blessings are too many to count, so we must be thankful for everything He has given us. We thank Allah (SWT) with our words and with our deeds.

quran.text: And Allah has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing, and He made for you hearing and vision and intellect that perhaps you would be grateful.

learn.title: Stay away from what Allah has forbidden
learn.html: What is forbidden (haram) brings harm – to each person and to everyone around us.

quran.text: …and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

learn.title: Ask for forgiveness and repent
learn.html: We ask Allah for forgiveness (istighfar) every day, and we repent (tawbah) when we make a mistake.

quran.text: But Allah would not punish them while you, [O Muhammad], are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.

learn.alt: A person walking along a path at a crossroads
learn.caption: The Straight Path

learn.html: When we fulfil our duties to Allah (SWT) and keep away from what He has forbidden, we walk on the Straight Path and earn His pleasure and happiness in this world and the next. The straight path of a Muslim is the path of doing what Allah commands and avoiding what He forbids.

practice.prompt: Is this duty fard (strict) or wajib?

practice.prompt: Tap everything that helps us fulfil our duties to Allah, then tap Check.

options.text: Staying away from what is forbidden

options.why: We do our duties for Allah, not to be seen by others.
Anyone can fulfil their duties to Allah – rich or poor.

questions.q: What are the strict Islamic duties (fard)?
options: Shahadah, salah, fasting, zakah and Hajj

questions.q: What does it mean that a duty is wajib?
options: It is not commanded as strictly as fard, but we should still do it
We never have to do it
It is the same as fard

questions.q: How does salah help the person who prays?
options: It keeps us away from what is bad

questions.q: Why did Allah command these duties?
options: They make our hearts pure and our character better

questions.q: What does being Allah’s servant mean?
options: Being the freest being on Earth

practice.title: Tasks and talking
prompts: 💭 How do you feel when you fulfil a duty to Allah (SWT) – for example when you pray Maghrib or fast a day of Ramadan? And how do you feel when you miss one you could have done?
✏️ Choose a task: list the duties Allah has given every Muslim.
✏️ Choose a task: how do you remember Allah (SWT) – how do you make dhikr?
